conflicts.subject: deal
conflicts.detail: Deal primary keys differ (A: integer, B: unknown)
solutions: Pick one key type for the merged entity and re-key the other source's rows
Keep a legacy_id column holding the old key during migration
conflicts.recommended: Use one key type (uuid is usual for merged data) and add a legacy_id column while migrating

resolution.decision: uuid (stored as text) for every unified Deal; each imported row keeps legacy_source ('A' or 'B') and legacy_id (A's integer id; B's id as text, type unknown) during and after migration; Contact is re-keyed the same way so Deal.contact_id is uuid

conflicts.subject: deal-stages
conflicts.detail: A's stages are lead, qualified, proposal, won, lost (fixed); B's default stages are new, contacted, negotiating, closed (caller-supplied). Existing stage values do not match, and B's 'closed' does not say whether the deal was won or lost.
solutions: One configurable stage table seeded with A's stages; map B's values new->lead, contacted->qualified, negotiating->proposal, and keep 'closed' as an extra closed stage with outcome 'unspecified'
Seed with B's stages and map A's won and lost both to closed (loses the outcome)
Keep two separate pipelines, one per source
conflicts.recommended: One configurable stage table seeded with A's five stages plus a 'closed' stage (outcome unspecified) for B's closed deals, so no stage value is lost or invented; users can reclassify those deals later

resolution.decision: Accept the recommendation: configurable Stage table seeded with lead, qualified, proposal, won, lost plus closed (outcome unspecified) for B's closed deals

conflicts.subject: deal-owner
conflicts.detail: B's reminders email deal['owner_email'], but A's deals have no owner at all and neither app has users or authentication, so reminders cannot work for A's deals until an owner exists.
solutions: Add a User entity and a required Deal.owner_id; B's owner_email values become users; A's deals are assigned to an owner the user names at migration
Keep a free-text owner_email on Deal and leave A's deals without reminders
conflicts.recommended: Add User and Deal.owner_id; create users from B's distinct owner_email values; assign A's existing deals to one default owner chosen by the user before migration

resolution.decision: Add User and required Deal.owner_id; create users from B's distinct owner_email values; A's existing deals get a default owner the user names before migration

conflicts.subject: deal.stage
conflicts.detail: Deal.stage types differ (A: text, B: unknown)
solutions: Choose the wider type and convert the narrower data
Split into two fields if they mean different things
conflicts.recommended: One type per field; convert in a migration

resolution.decision: Deal.stage becomes stage_id (uuid, FK to Stage); A's text values map 1:1 to the seeded stages; B's values map new->lead, contacted->qualified, negotiating->proposal, closed->'closed' (outcome unspecified); any other B value is imported as an extra configured stage, never dropped

conflicts.subject: deal.title
conflicts.detail: Deal.title types differ (A: text, B: unknown)
solutions: Choose the wider type and convert the narrower data
Split into two fields if they mean different things
conflicts.recommended: One type per field; convert in a migration

resolution.decision: Deal.title is text, not null, max 200; B's values (type unknown, used as text) are cast with str() on import and the dry run reports any that are empty or not strings

conflicts.subject: deal-contact
conflicts.detail: A's deals link to a contact; B's deals have no contact, so B's deals arrive without one.
solutions: Keep Deal.contact_id nullable
Create a placeholder contact for B's deals
conflicts.recommended: Keep Deal.contact_id nullable (it already is in A's schema); show 'no contact' in the UI

resolution.decision: Deal.contact_id stays nullable; B's deals import with no contact

conflicts.subject: reminders-on-closed-deals
conflicts.detail: B's reminder job does not exclude closed deals, so after the merge won and lost deals would be emailed about forever; it also re-sends on every run.
solutions: Skip deals in stages whose outcome is won, lost or unspecified-closed, and dedupe on (deal, moved_at)
Keep B's behaviour
conflicts.recommended: Skip closed stages and send at most one reminder per deal per idle period

resolution.decision: Reminders skip stages with a closed outcome and dedupe on (deal_id, moved_at)

conflicts.subject: deal
conflicts.detail: Deal exists in A:Deal, B:Deal; fields not shared: contact_id (only A), moved_at (only B), owner_email (only B), value_cents (only A)
solutions: Merge into one table holding the fields kept features need
Keep separate tables if the two only share a name, and rename one
conflicts.recommended: Merge into one entity; list every field's origin in architecture.json

resolution.decision: Merge A:Deal and B:Deal into one Deal entity; field origins listed in architecture.json

conflicts.subject: moved-at-timezone
conflicts.detail: B stores moved_at from datetime.utcnow(), a naive timestamp.
solutions: Store timezone-aware UTC; treat B's naive values as UTC on import
conflicts.recommended: Store timezone-aware UTC; treat B's naive values as UTC on import

resolution.decision: Store timezone-aware UTC; B's naive values are read as UTC on import; A's deals get moved_at = import time

conflicts.subject: merge-vs-moved-at
conflicts.detail: A's contact merge rewrites deals; if it touched moved_at it would reset B's staleness clock.
solutions: Merge changes only contact_id on deals
Treat a merge as a move
conflicts.recommended: Merge changes only contact_id; moved_at changes only on stage moves

resolution.decision: Contact merge changes only contact_id on deals; moved_at changes only on stage moves
